findings.summary: The pickable flag was copied onto RenderItem and tested from that snapshot in each PAL, but the pin re-walks scene.meshes on every pickAsync -- so a flag written after the last membership change would never have reached a pick. The predicate is now generated (pick_candidate, beside light_affects_mesh, gated on picking:gpu) and reads the live record; the lane and both hand-written guards are gone, and the 220 non-picking scenes no longer emit it.

The comment on the assignment site said the flag is read per draw and takes effect on the next frame, contradicting docs/fidelity.md in the same commit and the gate's own second probe, which measures the deferral. It was a leftover from before the measurement.

The two mesh flags open-coded the ceremony that recordFieldAssignments exists to declare -- engine resolution, compound rejection, the record[handle].field string. They are now two table rows, and the table gained the optional feature hook its sibling in properties.ts already had.

isLocationGlobal was a third copy of the bare-or-window global shape already inlined in isDeferredCallbackCall. One browserGlobalNamed helper now serves both, routed through isDefaultBrowserGlobal so a lexical shadow cannot be mistaken for the global and globalThis is an accepted host.

The fidelity note claimed the port and the pin defer a bare visible write identically. The pin also tests visible inside drawList, which render-task.ts calls on the direct and transparent bindings every frame OUTSIDE the bundle-record branch -- so the deferral is the opaque bucket's alone and this port applies it wider. The claim is now scoped.

Folding visible into plan membership also cost the picker its candidates: the pass walks the plan, which dropped an invisible mesh, where gpu-picker.ts never tests visibility. Rather than record the divergence, the test moved out of build_render_plan into the draw-list seam, so the plan stays complete and a hidden mesh is a pick candidate as it is upstream. A fourth probe measures it.

That move turned a loud failure into a silent wrong draw: both PALs' depth-only render-task path walks task.render_meshes and resolves against render_plan.items directly, consuming no draw list, and used to throw when a hidden mesh was absent. It now draws one. geometry-renderer-task.ts skips it at the draw, so the test became a generated mesh_draws predicate asked by append_draw and by both depth paths -- three consumers, which is the criterion pick_candidate set.

Dawn's per-frame mesh sync writes bone palettes and parent worlds unconditionally, so scene 34's three hidden meshes cost 12,384 bytes of writeBuffer per frame for meshes that never draw. SDL pays nothing because it pushes both per DRAW. Guarded on the same predicate, with the invariant that makes it sound recorded: the membership rebuild runs earlier in the same frame.

The merged nodeVisibility flag also drove the glTF loader's KHR_node_visibility cascade, so a scene writing mesh.visible while loading an asset without the extension would emit the per-node walk. The loader now takes an asset-only gltfNodeVisibility; the renderer and camera skips keep the merged value, and the inventory row became a checkedRow so the merge cannot drift from cli.ts.

docs/fidelity.md contradicted itself: one paragraph still said build_render_plan skips an invisible mesh, four lines above the paragraph saying testing at plan membership would have dropped one. Fixed, along with three other landmarks still reading "before the plan is built". The picking paragraph was drift -- its thesis was an agreement with the pin, which is not that page's subject -- so it shrank to the one port-specific clause and cross-links features.md, which owns the rule.

The gate's magenta diagnostic twin could only appear in a run that had already failed, and dataset.pickedHit already records the resolved name including "miss". Removed, along with dead x/z arguments the next line overwrote -- a shape the fourth probe then reintroduced and this pass removed again.

Gate hygiene: the header said "Three probes" with four listed and numbered them 1, 2, 4, 3; a comment saying "without a second marker in the scene" sat two lines below a new second marker; the 0.3125 pick ratio now records its measured overlap band [0.265, 0.334] and which direction fails silently rather than loudly, since that is the one that would quietly weaken the probe.
The new registry entry was spliced above the retire comment belonging to regression-material-falloff. The comment went back to its subject and the new gate got its own.

Shortening the gate's drain to the count its comment claimed made the native capture land before the marker appeared. Chasing that exposed a race the gate had been winning by luck: the pick runs on the setTimeout-0 continuation, which finish_frame drains at the END of a frame, after that frame's capture check -- so frame 0 could be captured before the drain existed. The gate now pins BBLITE_SCREENSHOT_FRAME.
